questions.stem: Correct NIST incident response lifecycle order:
questions.explanation: NIST SP 800-61: Preparation; Detection & Analysis; Containment, Eradication & Recovery; Post-Incident Activity.
Containment stops an active incident from spreading, buying time for eradication and recovery.

questions.stem: Removing malware and applying patches occurs during:
questions.explanation: Eradication removes the cause, deleting malware and closing exploited vulnerabilities, after containment limits damage.

choices.A: Identify gaps and improve future response

questions.explanation: Post-incident reviews drive continuous improvement of response processes and preventive controls.

questions.stem: A PRIMARY Preparation phase responsibility is:

choices.D: Establishing IR policies, teams, tools, and communication plans

questions.explanation: Preparation builds IR capability before incidents: creating teams, developing playbooks, deploying detection tools.

choices.A: Evidence is collected as quickly as possible
choices.B: All evidence is encrypted before law enforcement
choices.C: Evidence is documented so its integrity is unquestionable in legal proceedings

questions.explanation: Chain of custody documents who collected, handled, and analysed evidence, proving it is admissible in court.

questions.stem: Unusual login patterns and new admin accounts are examples of:
questions.explanation: IoCs are forensic artefacts suggesting potential compromise, evidence of attacker activity warranting investigation.

choices.A: 24/7 monitoring and initial triage of security alerts

questions.explanation: A SOC monitors security events continuously, performing initial triage to determine incidents requiring escalation.

questions.stem: A forensic analyst's FIRST action at a compromised workstation:

choices.C: Photograph the screen and document system state before touching anything

questions.explanation: Documenting the current state first preserves volatile evidence. Rebooting or scanning destroys RAM contents and alters timestamps.

choices.B: Critical business functions continue during and after a disruptive event

questions.explanation: BCP plans to maintain or restore critical processes during disruptions, minimising operational downtime.
